observations: body L1: «احد» is printed with an elongated join (kashīda) after the ḥāʾ, not transcribed.
body L2: the hamza of «نَاءَ» and its fatḥa are cast as one sort (4.0 by 4.6 points).
body L4: «نَيِّرٌ» is printed with an elongated join (kashīda) after the nūn, not transcribed.
body L5, L10: «٢٤٥–٢٧٤» (L5) and «Bouché–Leclercq» (L10) are printed with an en dash (5.4 points).
body L14: the sign after «au plur.» is a heavy cross with an open lozenge at its centre (9.0 by 8.7 points), transcribed ✜.

body L18, L19: the Syriac words are set in the West Syriac type with the vowel signs taken from the Greek letters: «ܢܰܝܙܟܳܐ» (L18) has the pthāḥā on the nun and the zqāpā on the kaph; «ܢܝ̈ܙܟܐ» (L19) has only the two points of the plural over the yudh; «ܢܰܒܪܶ̈ܫܬܳܢܳܝܶܐ» has the pthāḥā on the nun, the rbāṣā and the two points of the plural on the rish (the dot of the rish is one of them), the zqāpā on the taw and on the second nun, and the rbāṣā on the yudh.
body L21: the comma after «هُبُوطٌ» is printed small (1.2 by 1.5 points); it reaches 0.5 point below the baseline, as a comma does, while the full points of the page stand on it.
body L23, L25, L26: the hyphens of the line numbers «1-2», «4-7» (L25) and «18-21» (L26) are printed short, like points (1.6-1.8 points); that of «14-15» (L23) is 3.0 points long.
body L24: «180°–270» is printed without the degree sign after 270.
body L35: «وكَدْخُداهًا» has the fatḥa on the kāf, the sukun on the dāl, the ḍamma on the khāʾ and the fatḥatān on the hāʾ; «هيلاجًا» has only the fatḥatān.

notes_left L1, L3: the third figure of «2360» (L3) is a 6 whose ball terminal touches the bowl and closes a small upper counter, as in the 6 of «1906» on p. 354; the 8 of «1895» (L1) has two round counters.
